user.title: Connect your XPENG vehicle
user.description:
Use a DEDICATED XPENG account that has been shared to your car - NOT your primary account. XPENG allows one active session per account, so signing in here logs your phone app out repeatedly.

Most accounts are gated by XPENG's slider captcha, which this screen cannot show, so "Import tokens from the onboarding tool" is the route that always completes.

data_description.auth_method: Import tokens is the reliable choice - see above. The next screen asks for the VIN only if the method you pick needs one.

google.title: Sign in with Google
google.description:
Sign in with Google to renew XPENG credentials.

**This path is not captcha-free.** XPENG applies the same slider captcha to the account after the Google sign-in, and that challenge cannot be solved from inside Home Assistant. If the sign-in is refused with a captcha error, run tools/onboard_email_login.py instead and use the "Import tokens from the onboarding tool" method.

**If a browser cannot deliver the callback** (on a Mac with the XPENG app installed the link opens the app; without it Google bounces to the homepage and the code is lost), run the helper instead:

`swift tools/oauth_capture.swift`

It opens the system sign-in window, captures the callback, and prints `VERIFIER:` and `CALLBACK:`. Paste the callback URL below and the verifier into the second field.

**Otherwise**, open this link and sign in, then paste the redirect URL:

{url}

email_password.title: Email sign-in
email_password.description:
Use a DEDICATED XPENG account that has been shared to your car - do NOT use your primary account. Signing in here creates a second client on the same account, and XPENG only allows one active session, so your phone app will get logged out repeatedly. Create a new XPENG account, share the car to it from your main account in the app, then sign in here with that one.

XPENG gates most accounts with a slider captcha, and that challenge can only be cleared by a human dragging it in a real browser - Home Assistant cannot do that. If this sign-in is refused as captcha-gated, stop here: run tools/onboard_email_login.py on a machine with a browser and use the "Import tokens from the onboarding tool" method instead.

data_description.vin: The 17-character VIN of your vehicle. It decides this entry's entity ids, so a wrong one creates a second set pointing at nothing.

import_tokens.title: Import onboarding tokens
import_tokens.description:
Both files must come from the SAME run of the onboarding tool: the tenant carries the deviceId the tokens are sealed against, so a pair from different runs is rejected.

On a machine with a browser: `pip install cryptography`, extract the mTLS certificates from an APK (step 2), then run `python3 tools/onboard_email_login.py --email YOU@example.com --save --mqtt` - it prompts for the password and needs one slider drag. Or let the renewal app mint the pair with the solver, which needs no desktop at all.

Paste both files below, or give their paths if they are already on this host.

{pair_search}

command_mode.title: What may this integration do to the car?
command_mode.description:
This is a ceiling for the whole integration, not a user permission: it applies to automations, scripts, voice assistants and access tokens too. The account credentials are the same at every level - the point is that a leaked token or a shared dashboard cannot unlock the car.

It does not stop an administrator (they can change this setting) and it does not stop anyone who can already read or write your Home Assistant configuration. You can change it later under Configure > Command permissions.

error.invalid_client_id: Client ID must be in format xmart:app:userId:deviceUUID
error.cannot_connect: Unable to connect to XPENG MQTT broker
error.login_failed: Login failed. Check your email and password.
error.invalid_code: Could not find an auth code in that URL. Copy the full address-bar URL after signing in.
error.captcha_gated: XPENG is asking for its slider captcha, and that challenge can only be cleared by a human dragging it in a real browser - Home Assistant cannot do that. Run tools/onboard_email_login.py on a machine with a browser (the tool opens XPENG's slider; drag it once), then add the integration again with the "Import tokens from the onboarding tool" method and paste the two files it wrote.
error.invalid_tokens_json: That is not valid JSON, so it cannot be the xpeng_tokens.json the onboarding tool wrote. Paste the whole file exactly as the tool saved it.
error.invalid_tokens: The token data is missing something required: it must contain accessToken, and either an mqttAccount clientId or a uid. Re-run the onboarding tool and use the files from that same run.
error.invalid_tokens_path: Could not read that xpeng_tokens.json path on the Home Assistant host. Check the path, or paste the file contents instead.
error.invalid_tenant_json: That is not valid JSON, so it cannot be the xpeng_tenant.json the onboarding tool wrote. Paste the whole file exactly as the tool saved it.
error.invalid_tenant: The tenant data is missing something required: it must contain deviceId and a non-empty keys pool, and every key must be base64 in the format the onboarding tool writes. Re-run the onboarding tool and use the tenant file from that same run - the tokens and tenant are a matched pair.
error.invalid_tenant_path: Could not read that xpeng_tenant.json path on the Home Assistant host. Check the path, or paste the file contents instead.
error.invalid_vin: The token file carries no VIN, and none was entered. Enter the 17-character VIN of the vehicle these tokens belong to.

data.capture_enabled: Record raw MQTT frames to a file
data.legacy_entities: Keep legacy buttons and duplicate sensors
data.enable_vehicle_card: Install and manage the XPENG Vehicle dashboard card

data_description.command_mode: Read only, Safe, Safe Plus and Full access are presets; Custom opens a second screen and lets you set each capability group to Full, Read only or Disabled. An install that has never been configured stays at Full access, so changing this cannot take a capability away from an automation by surprise.
data_description.allow_wake: Only affects waking a sleeping car for a full state update. Charge and drive polls are unaffected because the car is already awake.
data_description.scan_interval: How often to query the vehicle state via MQTT (10-3600 seconds). The query force-uploads only while the car is charging or driving, so it never wakes a sleeping car; a charging hint raises polling to this cadence.
data_description.parked_scan_interval: Passive query interval while parked (60-7200 seconds). Also slows the REST poll while parked. Never wakes the car.
data_description.mqtt_refresh_interval: Retry cadence for a disconnected MQTT client, and the age bound behind the credentials sensor (10-300 seconds). Credentials are minted on demand before a connection; this never rotates a live session.
data_description.rest_scan_interval: How often to poll the REST API for the vehicle image and XOS version (60-3600 seconds). Message Centre notifications have their own interval.
data_description.mqtt_listener_enabled: Subscribe to additional MQTT topics beyond the primary vehicle state topic
data_description.mqtt_listener_topics: Additional MQTT topics to subscribe to (one per line, or comma-separated). Supports MQTT wildcards (+ and #), and expands the device-id and user-id placeholders described under MQTT listener in the documentation - e.g. the app's device push channel. The listener sensor records whether the broker granted each topic.
data_description.mqtt_topic_discovery: Automatically try subscribing to known XPENG broker topics (CanPack, StatPack, etc.) to discover accessible data
data_description.capture_enabled: Write every frame from the topics below to a binary journal for offline decoding, without decoding or updating entities per frame.
data_description.capture_path: Where captures are written. Use a path outside /config - /share is not carried into every backup. Falls back to <config>/xpeng-can if it cannot be created.
data_description.capture_topics: One per line or comma-separated; MQTT wildcards (+, #) are supported. Leave empty for the known CAN topics.
data_description.token_file: Path to login tokens JSON from CLI login script. Only needed if not using in-HA login.
data_description.tenant_file: Path to cached tenant data. Auto-fetched if missing.
data_description.cert_dir: Absolute path to the directory holding ca-chain.crt, client-cert-0.pem and client-key.pem. Default: /config/custom_components/xpeng/certs.
data_description.iccid: TBox SIM ICCID. Optional: leave it blank and this sensor is not created; set it and the integration adds one diagnostic sensor showing the value. No app-tier API exposes it, so read it on the car's screen by entering *#9925*131# in the head-unit dialler.
data_description.usable_battery_kwh: Set this to your car's pack, from the figure it is known by. A VIN gives the model family only, so nothing can pick this for you. Usable kWh: G6 66.0 pack = 65.3 | G6 68.5 = 67.8 | G6 80.8 = 80.0 | G6 87.5 (MY24 NMC) = 87.5 | G9 78.2 = 75.8 | G9 79.0 = 78.2 | G9 93.1 (LFP, MY25 on) = 92.2 | G9 98.0 (NMC, MY23-24) = 93.1. Only the parked-consumption estimate uses it.
data_description.notification_poll_interval: How often to poll XPENG's Message Centre for notifications. Six requests per poll, one per category; a notification cannot arrive sooner than this. The sensor records the real delay as `delay_s`.
data_description.teslamate_provider_enabled: Run a Tesla-compatible API on the port below so TeslaMate can log this car as if it were a Tesla. Read-only: no command routes are served, so this cannot move or unlock the car. Off by default.
data_description.teslamate_provider_port: The port the provider listens on, reachable from the TeslaMate container or host. Must not be 8123 (Home Assistant itself). 8200 is the default so it does not collide with TeslaMate's own web UI on 4000.
data_description.teslamate_provider_token: Shared secret. Copy this into TeslaMate's TOKEN environment variable; TeslaMate sends it as a bearer token on every request and the provider rejects anything else. Generated on first view - change it and TeslaMate must be re-signed-in.
data_description.legacy_entities: Turn off for unified covers and charging switch. Retires old paired buttons and duplicate sensors; update automations first. Turn on to restore legacy entities.
data_description.charge_port_controls: Turn off for a manual charge flap. The charge-port cover still reports state, without open/close actions.
data_description.enable_vehicle_card: Optional, off by default. Registers one shared card resource, updates it with the integration, and migrates matching legacy /local/ card resources. In YAML-resource mode it loads the module globally; remove any old manual XPENG resource from YAML once. Turning this off for all vehicles, or removing the last opted-in vehicle, removes the managed resource. Dashboard layouts are never edited.

groups.title: Command permissions by capability group
groups.description:
Each group is independent. Full allows its commands, Read only keeps its entities and their state but refuses every command, and Disabled does not create them at all.

The groups are split by what an action does to the car rather than by subsystem, which is why locking and unlocking are not in the same one: locking only removes access, unlocking hands the car over.

data_description.queries: State updates, wake, X-Guard query, OTA check, HVAC schedule listing, navigation cards, snapshot capture.
data_description.comfort: Cabin climate and modes (including Pet mode and Sterilisation), defrost, seat and steering-wheel heating/ventilation, and HVAC schedules. Fan-speed control is withheld.
data_description.charging: Start and stop charging, charge limit, and both charge port doors.
data_description.securing: Lock, close windows, close the trunk, arm X-Guard. These only ever reduce access to the car, so they cannot compromise it.
data_description.access: Unlock, open the trunk, open or vent the windows, disarm X-Guard. This is the group that hands the car over.
data_description.power: The V2L outlet in the trunk and its auto-off timer.
data_description.firmware: Trigger, cancel and enable automatic OTA upgrades, and send upgrade feedback.
data_description.advanced: send_raw_mqtt plus X-Combo scenes. Raw commands can express any other group, including unlock, and scenes are opaque server-side programs - keep these at Full access unless you know why.

error.cert_files_missing: One or more certificate files are missing from that directory. It must contain ca-chain.crt, client-cert-0.pem and client-key.pem.
error.token_required: A token of at least 8 characters is required: the provider is reachable on the network and TeslaMate authenticates with this value.
error.port_conflict: Port 8123 is Home Assistant's own HTTP server. Pick another port, e.g. 8200.

confirm.title: Re-import XPENG tokens
confirm.description:
The XPENG credentials for **{entry}** (VIN `{vin}`) expired and could not be renewed automatically, so the vehicle entities have stopped updating.

Home Assistant cannot log in on its own: XPENG gates sign-in with a slider captcha that only a human dragging it in a real browser can clear.

**1.** On a computer, run the onboarding tool again:

```
python3 tools/onboard_email_login.py \
    --email YOUR_EMAIL --password 'YOUR_PASSWORD' \
    --save --mqtt
```

Drag the slider once when the browser opens.

**2.** Paste the two files it wrote below, then submit. Both are needed: the tenant carries the device identity the tokens were sealed to.

Full walkthrough: https://github.com/xpengtoolkit/xpengtoolkit#setup

confirm.description:
XPENG rejected the stored credentials for **{entry}** (VIN `{vin}`), and they could not be renewed automatically.

This usually means the pair is no longer valid, or that the tokens and the tenant came from different onboarding runs - they must be imported together, because the tenant records the device identity the tokens were sealed against.

Re-run `tools/onboard_email_login.py`, then paste the fresh pair below. See https://github.com/xpengtoolkit/xpengtoolkit#setup
